title: at edit is kind-blind and the refusal's own remedy walks a non-test row into carrying both file and prose, which at lint has no rule for
body:
`at edit` is KIND-BLIND in both directions, and the route into the resulting contradictory row is the tool's OWN refusal remedy.

MEASURED by ic 2026-08-29 against the delivered pair `30a2dd81`, in a throwaway `intent init` fixture, never the live estate. Independently reproduced by vc in a separate fixture under a fake HOME, both directions.

## The route in is the tool's own advice

`at new` on a taken id refuses correctly at rc=1 -- that part works and is not the defect. Its remedy says, on a row of ANY kind:

    To re-cite it, `intent at edit ST0001 AT-01.1 --file <path>`

The remedy is kind-blind. On a `kind: non-test` row, `--file` is the wrong flag: `--prose`'s own help, and `docs/reference/intent-at.md`'s flag table in the same words, define prose as "What a non-test row asserts INSTEAD OF a file".

Following the remedy verbatim returns rc=0 (`ok: AT-01.1 re-cited`) and leaves:

    {"id":"AT-01.1","kind":"non-test","file":"some/test/path.rs","prose":"original prose","status":"n-a"}

Both fields present, on a kind whose vocabulary says they are alternatives.

## It is the verb, not the flag -- the mirror confirms it

`at edit --prose` on a `kind: test` row also returns rc=0:

    {"id":"AT-01.2","kind":"test","file":"real/test.rs","prose":"eyeballed it, no file involved","status":"green"}

So `at edit` never consults the row's kind when deciding whether a field applies. Neither direction is refused and neither is warned about.

## `at lint` has no rule for it, and this was measured with a WORKING instrument

Both rows were driven OFF `to-write` first (`at na` and `at green`), because `at lint` exempts `to-write` from L2/L3 -- so a `conform` verdict on to-write rows means EXEMPT, not CHECKED, and would have been a blind green.

With the exemption gone, `at lint ST0001` reports exactly one finding -- `AT-01.2 cites a file that does not exist` -- and rc=1. That rc=1 is the positive control: lint is not stuck-green, it fires on this very corpus, and it still says nothing about either row carrying both fields.

## Why medium rather than minor

No data is destroyed and no exit code lies. What makes it worth a row is the path: the operator most likely to produce the impossible state is the one who did what the error message told them to do. A defect you can only reach by ignoring the tool is a sharp edge; one you reach by obeying it is a trap.

## Two candidate fixes, not ruled between

1. Make the remedy kind-aware -- name `--prose` for a non-test row and `--file` for a test row. Cheapest, and closes the route that produces the state in practice.
2. Make `at edit` refuse a field that does not apply to the row's kind, and give `at lint` a rule for the both-fields state. Closes the state itself rather than one route to it.

They are not alternatives in the long run; (1) without (2) leaves the state reachable by hand.

## Related, not duplicated

`kind` is unwritable on both edit verbs by declared design (`8aebe2ce`), so an operator who reaches this state cannot correct it by changing the row's kind. That is a separate stated hole, and it is what makes the contradictory row sticky.


## Fix (2) is BLOCKED ON AC-04.6, not sequenced after it -- and a live row is already trapped (dc, 2026-09-01, ruled by vc)

**READ THIS BEFORE TAKING FIX (2). ON ITS OWN IT IS A REGRESSION, AND THE SECTION ABOVE READS AS IF IT WERE SAFE.**

Fix (2) makes `at edit` refuse a field that does not apply to the row's kind. Apply it to a row that is ALREADY mis-kinded and `--file` becomes refused, while there is no `--kind`, no re-mint and no delete. **The row freezes permanently in the contradictory state.** Fix (2) closes the LAST door that can touch those fields on a mis-kinded row.

So it is not an ordering preference. **Fix (2) may not land until kind conversion exists, which is `ST0056` AC-04.6 -- mutation completeness, D32, *every state an entity can enter, it can leave*.** Ruled by vc 2026-09-01 on this measurement. **Fix (1) -- kind-aware remedy text on the refusal -- is safe alone and remains takeable at any time.**

### The stickiness this issue already names is EXHAUSTIVE, and that was driven rather than assumed

The `Related, not duplicated` section above already states that `kind` is unwritable on both edit verbs by declared design. **What it does not establish is that no OTHER route exists**, which is what makes fix (2) fatal rather than merely inconvenient. Driven in a throwaway `intent init` fixture under a fake HOME, never the live estate -- the third independent reproduction of this issue, after ic's and vc's:

| door | result |
| --- | --- |
| `ac edit --kind` | rc=1 `unexpected argument '--kind' found` -- clap-level, the flag does not exist |
| `at edit --kind` | rc=1 `unexpected argument '--kind' found` -- clap-level, the flag does not exist |
| `at new <taken id>` | rc=1 `a create must not replace it` -- refused by design |
| `at lint --fix` | rc=1 `not implemented in v3` |
| an AT delete verb | **DOES NOT EXIST** -- the family is list/lint/green/red/na/new/edit |

`--kind` is settable at MINT on both entities and changeable nowhere. The both-fields state was reproduced identically: `at edit --file` on a `kind: non-test` row returns rc=0 `ok: re-cited`, leaving kind=non-test with file AND prose both set, and `at lint` then reports `conform` -- driven off `to-write` to `n-a` first, so lint was CHECKING that row rather than exempting it.

### A live victim exists in this repo, which every prior measurement here was a fixture

`ST0056` AT-07.7 is `(non-test)` and carries a test result, reported by `intent doctor` as `model-inconsistent`. Its instrument genuinely runs -- `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/claude_doors_installed_check.sh`, two-sided, the published artefact scoring 0/5 doors reachable against the tree's 5/5 -- so the truthful repair is kind `non-test -> test`, **and no shipped verb can perform it.**

**The row stays red and inconsistent by vc's ruling 2026-09-01.** The reachable exit, `at na`, was refused on the ground that it records *n/a -- nothing ran* about a row whose instrument demonstrably runs: it would trade a true inconsistency for a false statement, and make the doctor finding disappear while the gap it evidences stays exactly as open. The finding is AC-04.6's evidence and is left standing deliberately.

### The general form, since the specific one nearly got built

**A refusal added to a surface that has no inverse is a ONE-WAY DOOR.** The failure is not writing the wrong remedy; it is scoping a remedy to the reported bug and closing the last escape hatch on the way past. Cheap detection, and it costs one question: **before adding a refusal, name the verb that undoes the state it will now trap. If there is none, that is welding rather than hardening.**
